# Draft:Eleanor Clarke Slagle Lectureship Award

Eleanor Clarke Slagle Lectureship Award
Eleanor Clarke Slagle Lectureship Award
The Elanor Clarke Slagle Lectureship Award was established in 1954 as a memorial to Eleanor Clarke Slagle, it is considered as the highest academic award of the AOTA. The purpose of this award is to honor a member of AOTA who has contributed to development of the profession's body of knowledge.
Requirements
To be eligible for this award, The nominee should have made an important contribution to occupational therapy by improving its ideas, methods, or practices in a way that helps education or patient care as well as long term commitment to sharing their work through publishing, presenting, teaching, or mentoring others.
Volunteer organizational leadership, like taking on leadership roles in professional organizations, like AOTA for example, as a volunteer, it also includes guiding initiatives or helping the organization grow.
